content.comment_body: Hello, I'm trying to measure the resistance value of a potentiometer (0 to 100 kOhm) using my [product_name]. I attempted to use the analog inputs, but their resistance is about 73.2 kOhm, which causes problems when measuring the voltage drop across the potentiometer. I need a resolution of 1 kOhm. I also tried using the 0...20mA function, but the current is too low for accurate measurement. Does anyone have suggestions? Thanks for your assistance :-)

Just a note: the input resistance of [product_name] isn't exactly 73.2 kOhm. My recommendation is to use an electronic amplifier or signal amplifier. The input resistance of the amplifier should be at least 10 MOhm; this ensures your measurement error stays below 1 kOhm when working with a potentiometer in the 0 - 100 kOhm range. If possible, an input resistance of 100 MOhm is even better. You can set the amplifier output to 0-10 V, which connects directly to the DC input of [product_name].

analysis.insight_summary: Users faced substantial challenges trying to directly measure a potentiometer's resistance using the analog input of [product_name], mainly due to the high input resistance (around 73.2 kOhm) causing inaccuracies. Both voltage and current measurement options were found to be insufficient, prompting recommendations for using an external signal amplifier to improve measurement accuracy.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the analog input of [product_name] to measure potentiometer resistance accurately, with good resolution and minimal error, and ideally without needing extra hardware.
